So a PoC that sets SIZ `Xsiz=32, XOsiz=17` (or `Ysiz=32,YOsiz=17`) may be the known vulnerability and would be fixed by patch. This could be better than random qmfbid assertion. Let's investigate.\n\nThe assertion `jas_seq2d_create xstart <= xend` means decoder created a matrix with negative dimensions after tile component bounds computed. The root cause is invalid SIZ parameters where image offset > extent. Fixed version likely checks SIZ parameters:\n```\nif (siz->xsiz <= siz->xosiz || siz->ysiz <= siz->yosiz) ...\n```\nWhich CVE? Could be CVE-2016-8883 \"Heap-based buffer overflow in jpc_tsfb_synthesize...\" or CVE-2016-8692. But regardless, patched variants might reject invalid SIZ and not assert. This is a strong candidate.\n\nLet's create minimal JPC with only SIZ (plus EOC?) where SIZ has Xsiz=32, XOsiz=17 and no tiles. But valid base codestream includes many markers; a simpler crafted SIZ with bad geometry might crash earlier. We can test creating a minimal JPC: SOC (ff4f), SIZ (ff51 length 41?) with fields Xsiz=32, XOsiz=17, rest 0, then EOC. But decoder may reject missing COD/QCD etc before reaching geometry. Let's test."}}
